judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 (rank 2) Content Standards in Strand 4: Writing, so the grain and statement type match. B3.4.4.1 'Draw and label simple pictures' (Sub-Strand 4: Labelling items; excerpted indicator context 'Make a list of objects found in the environment') requires learners to produce isolated written words/labels attached to drawings — a word-level writing and vocabulary-in-writing task. B3.4.5.1 'Write accurately using acquired vocabulary and knowledge of grammar' (Sub-Strand 5: Writing Simple Words and Sentences) extends that word-level output to accurate connected writing that applies acquired vocabulary plus grammatical knowledge, a substantively broader and more complex demand. Facility with labelling/listing object vocabulary in writing plausibly supports success in writing accurately with that acquired vocabulary, supporting a same-rank first-to-second developmental direction on content, not merely on shared code prefix (b3.4), shared Strand/Grade ancestors, page proximity, or the single shared token 'and', which alone would not suffice. Evidence limits: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 35 omitted items), no Learning Components were supplied, and B3.4.5.1 is a merged 'CONT'D' continuation record with slightly varying wording ('acquired vocabulary and knowledge of grammar' vs 'word recognition and knowledge of grammar and vocabulary'), so confidence is moderate rather than high.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (rank 1, no grade gap) under the same Strand 1: Oral Language but different sub-strands: B2.1.4.1 'Respond to stories' (Sub-Strand 4: Story Telling) and B2.1.2.1 'Show understanding of a variety of literary pieces' (Sub-Strand 2: Rhymes, whose indicator context concerns interpreting rhymes and tongue-twisters in own words). They share substantive coherence as oral-language comprehension and response to spoken literary forms, so the skills meaningfully reinforce each other. However, neither statement's bounded evidence shows one being a deepening, extension, or enabling capability for the other at the same grade rank: responding to stories and interpreting rhymes/tongue-twisters are parallel applications in distinct sub-strands, and the nomination signals (shared ancestors, adjacent pages, one shared trigram 'rie', weak 'b2.1' code prefix) are not semantic developmental evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and neither carries Learning Components, so any finer-grained dependency could not be assessed.

B1.2.7.2.1 addresses demonstrating understanding of the purpose and features of narrative texts; B1.2.7.2.6 addresses identifying the structure of a story (beginning, middle, end). These are substantively coherent — story structure is one concrete aspect of narrative-text features, and the shared 'comprehension' LC tag reflects genuine narrative-comprehension coherence rather than mere wording overlap. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Basic 3 Indicators in Strand 1: Oral Language at the same coordinate rank (BASIC 3, rank 2), so no lower-to-higher developmental ordering is available from the coordinate and no same-rank evidence establishes that one is a precondition for the other. They sit under different Sub-Strands and different Content Standards: B3.1.7.1.1 (Listening Comprehension; LCs 'Listen to information texts', 'Interact actively within information texts') versus B3.1.8.1.1 (Asking and Answering Questions; LCs 'Ask questions for clarifications about given topics', 'Answer questions for clarifications about given topics'). The coherence is substantive rather than merely lexical: active oral interaction with information texts and clarifying question-and-answer exchange are complementary oral-interaction capabilities that mutually reinforce comprehension of spoken/expository content, which supports a symmetric relatesTo rather than a directional claim. Shared code prefix, adjacent source pages, and token overlap limited to 'and' were treated as nomination signals only. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source evidence items each) and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, but the statement text, Sub-Strand scope, and Learning Components present are sufficient and non-conflicting for this symmetric judgment.
